jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Learning-Based Multi-Agent Control under Uncertainty
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at the Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a postdoc in learning-based multi-agent control under uncertainty, with applications to autonomous multi-robot systems operating in dynamic and uncertain environments, as per February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is available for a period of 2 years.

Your work tasks   The position focuses on fundamental research in learning-based planning and control of interacting autonomous agents under uncertainty. You will develop new theoretical and algorithmic approaches for distributed and cooperative control, combining learning or online adaptation with principled treatment of safety, robustness, and performance. Research challenges include uncertain dynamics and disturbances, partial or noisy information, changing interactions between agents, and limited or unreliable communication.

A central part of the work will be to formulate rigorous methods and establish their properties, for example concerning stability, safety, constraint satisfaction, robustness, and convergence, where applicable. Depending on the research direction, the work may draw on learning-augmented model predictive control, safe reinforcement learning, data-driven modelling and safety mechanism (e.g. CBF), distributed optimization, or robust and adaptive control. You will develop reproducible numerical studies and simulations to examine the strengths, limitations, and scalability of the proposed methods.

The research will be carried out in the Horizon Europe ROX-6G project, where heterogeneous robot teams provide a compelling application for coordination under uncertain conditions and connectivity constraints. Although the position is primarily theoretical, you will collaborate with colleagues working on robotic implementation and will contribute to experimental validation. You will lead and co-author publications in international journals and conferences, engage with project partners, contribute to research planning and scientific discussions, and support knowledge exchange within the team.

Your competencies

We seek a researcher with a PhD in control engineering, robotics, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, or a closely related field, and a strong background in mathematical modelling, control, optimization, or multi-agent systems.

You should be able to formulate original research problems, develop and analyse rigorous methods, and demonstrate research quality through peer-reviewed scientific publications. Experience in learning-based control, robust or nonlinear control, distributed control, or decision-making under uncertainty is particularly relevant; expertise in every one of these areas is not expected.

You should have good scientific programming skills, for example in Python, MATLAB, or C++, and be able to evaluate algorithms systematically through simulation. We value independent research initiative, clear scientific writing, and the ability to work constructively with researchers from different disciplines and backgrounds. Experience with autonomous robots, ROS/ROS 2, multi-robot simulation, or physical robotic experiments will be considered an advantage, but is not a prerequisite for this primarily theory-oriented position. Excellent written and spoken English is required.

Who we are

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

The position is hosted in the Automation and Control Section, within a collaborative robotics research environment combining fundamental research with real-world applications.

In addition, you will work with an international team and research partners in ROX-6G, a European collaboration addressing autonomous robotic operations in demanding underground environments. Our research interests span safe and resilient decision-making, learning-enabled control, distributed multi-robot coordination, and validation in simulation and on robotic platforms. We encourage scientific independence, close exchange of ideas, and publication of high-quality research. More information: www.es.aau.dk.

Qualification requirements Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Senior CRM Analyst
jobs.description:
The banking and digital marketing landscape is shifting fast, and Danske Bank is moving with it. As a Senior CRM Analyst, you will shape how we reach over 200,000 small and mid-sized corporate customers across the Nordic countries through data-driven campaigns. You will apply your Adobe competencies to turn complex data into targeted campaigns and customer journeys. You will gain real ownership of your work, collaborate across borders, and grow your skills in a team that values curiosity and shared learning.

What you will be doing

You will join the BC Analytics & Insights team, a Nordic group working at the intersection of data, marketing, and commercial strategy. The team operates in an agile sprint environment and works closely with Marketing and Commercial Planners across Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland. Your work will directly support the Business Customers unit, helping ensure that campaigns and customer journeys are built on solid, well-structured data and audience logic.

More specifically, you will:

• Translate campaign briefs into technical campaign flows and audience logic in Adobe

• Build and process complex target groups for campaigns, customer journeys, and customer signals

• Support colleagues in Adobe usage as Danske Bank transitions from SAS360 to Adobe

• Collaborate with Marketing and Commercial Planners to identify relevant target groups

• Keep stakeholders informed on progress and ensure alignment with commercial strategies

About you

• Experience working with Adobe MarTech solutions

• Solid SQL skills and a structured, data-driven approach

• Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken

• Commercial mindset with the ability to translate business needs into data logic

• Comfortable working independently and managing multiple tasks

• Embrace change and integrate AI into your daily work

• Curious, open to questioning existing approaches, and willing to share knowledge with colleagues

Experience with B2B customers or the banking industry is a plus, as is familiarity with platform migration projects or working in agile teams with remote members across different countries.

What we offer you

This role is based in Denmark and follows a hybrid working model, with three to four days per week in the office to support collaboration and knowledge sharing. You will have genuine autonomy in your work and access to continuous learning opportunities that support your long-term development. The team is skilled, collaborative, and committed to doing good work together.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right move for you, we welcome your application. Feel free to reach out to Louise Nørsten, Head of Analytics & Pricing, at lnrs@danskebank.dk if you have any questions before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as.

jobs.occupation: Tax Manager - Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Are you ready to shape the tax function of an international shipping company?

Clipper is enhancing its internal tax capability as part of a continued focus on strengthening governance and decision support across the organisation. We are therefore looking for a dedicated and hands-on Tax Manager to be based at Clipper’s headquarters in Copenhagen.

Today, tax matters at Clipper are handled across Finance, Legal and external advisors. With increasing regulatory complexity and risk exposure, we are establishing a more formalized and proactive tax function. The Tax Manager will play a key role in building this capability and embedding robust tax governance across the organization.

You will report directly to the CFO and work closely with the Head of Legal & Corporate Affairs and Head of Controlling and external advisors.

What will be your responsibilities

You will be responsible for both strategic and operational tax matters across Clipper’s global activities. Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

• Establish and maintain Clipper’s tax governance framework, including a tax risk register and clear processes for identifying, assessing and managing tax risks.

• Review the tax implications of material transactions and challenge tax positions and advice from external advisors where relevant.

• Own and oversee transfer pricing policies, intercompany agreements, benchmarking and documentation.

• Monitor and manage cross-border tax matters, including withholding tax, freight tax and permanent establishment risks.

• Oversee compliance with Danish tonnage tax requirements, including calculations, documentation and relevant controls.

• Coordinate corporate tax, VAT and employment tax compliance and reporting across jurisdictions, ensuring timely filings and robust documentation.

• Advise on tax matters related to international employee mobility and contractor arrangements.

• Monitor relevant tax and regulatory developments, including OECD Pillar Two and environmental and emissions-related taxes, and assess their impact on Clipper.

• Act as Clipper’s internal tax expert and trusted sparring partner, advising management on tax implications of strategic and operational decisions.

What we are looking for

At Clipper, our employees shape our work environment, so bringing a positive attitude is essential.

• We imagine that you have a relevant educational background within finance, tax, business administration, law or similar, combined with solid experience in corporate and international tax.

• You have hands-on experience with tax governance and tax risk management, combined with strong knowledge of transfer pricing, cross-border taxation and international tax principles.

• You are comfortable working with external advisors while also challenging and validating tax positions when needed.

• You are structured and analytical, but also pragmatic and commercially minded.

• You enjoy taking ownership, working independently and turning complex tax matters into practical advice and solutions for the business.

• You communicate confidently across functions and levels of the organisation and are fluent in both Danish and English.

• Shipping experience, including knowledge of tonnage tax or other shipping-specific tax matters, is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Don’t meet every single requirement?

If you’re enthusiastic about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with each qualification, we still encourage you to apply. You could be the ideal candidate for this position, or for another opportunity with us.

What you will love about us

At Clipper, you will become part of a growing and professional work environment where we strive to be the best. We offer:

• A key role with significant influence on Clipper Bulk's tax framework and risk profile

• The opportunity to build and shape an internal tax function

• Close collaboration with senior management and exposure to strategic decision-making

• A welcoming and inclusive work environment with a variety of socal, sports, and cultural events throughout the year

• Attractive employee benefits, including pension, health, dental and critical ilness insurance

• Beautiful office facilities in Nordhavn, located near the metro with on-site paring, delicious lunch arangement and access to fitness facilities and a personal trainer.

Application and recruitment process

Please submit your CV and cover letter through our application portal by 22nd November 2026.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and interviews will be treated with full discretion.

The recruitment process consist of two interview rounds. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a first interview, while candidates progressing to the second round will be asked to complete a personality assessment beforehand. Confidential reference checks will be conducted for final candidates.

Learn more about Clipper at clipper-bulk.com, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

Clipper is an industry leader in dry bulk, an operator, a pool manager, and a specialist in steel services. We operate a modern fleet of approximately 120 handysize and supramax vessels, transporting a wide range of cargo from dry bulk to break bulk. Clipper is commercially headquartered in Copenhagen and employs a staff of around 100 onshore worldwide__. We are a global workplace built on five shared values: Dependable, Curious, Collaboration, Hands-on and Family. We believe in learning from one another and welcome people with a growth mindset and ambition.

Sustainability initiatives - we strive to make a positive impact. As a maritime player with a global presence at sea and onshore, we recognize our social, environmental, and ethical responsibility. We push for positive development by responsibly running our business and promoting sustainable business behavior in our network. Read more about sustainability initiatives on our website_.

jobs.occupation: Development Manager
jobs.description:
IST is looking for an experienced Development Manager who thrives at the intersection of technology, people, and delivery and who is ready to lead and evolve our development organization to the next level.

At IST, we’re not just building software—we’re shaping the future of education. Our digital tools connect schools, teachers, students, and families in smarter, more meaningful ways. With over five million users across Europe, our mission is clear: to make learning easier, more engaging, and more impactful for everyone.

Joining IST means working in an international, collaborative environment where your leadership and ideas make a real difference. You’ll guide and inspire development teams, influence technical direction, and contribute to products used by thousands of schools—while growing alongside experienced colleagues who are passionate about improving education.

Role overview

We are looking for a Development Manager who is passionate about people, software development and building high-performing engineering teams. In this role, you will lead and support a few development teams while working closely with Product Owners, Architects and other stakeholders to create high-quality software solutions.

As a Development Manager, your primary focus will be leadership, team development, delivery and creating an environment where engineers can thrive and do their best work. We also believe you are curious about emerging technologies and interested in how AI can support software development, collaboration and innovation.

Key responsibilities

• Lead, coach and support some development teams

• Foster a collaborative, inclusive and high-performing engineering culture

• Support team members in their professional growth and development

• Ensure effective ways of working, agile processes and continuous improvement

• Collaborate with Product Owners and other stakeholders to align priorities and deliveries

• Drive recruitment, onboarding and team development activities

• Help teams remove obstacles and improve delivery capabilities

• Follow up on team goals, performance, engagement and work environment

• Encourage experimentation and learning around new technologies, including AI-driven tools and workflows

Role qualifications

We believe you have the following experience, capabilities and personal skills to succeed in this role:

• A bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering or related field

• Previous experience in a leadership role within software development

• A background in software engineering or technical product development

• Strong communication and collaboration skills

• Experience working with agile development methodologies

• The ability to balance people management with business and delivery needs

• A coaching and supportive leadership style

• An interest in AI and how new technologies can improve the way teams work and deliver software

• Fluent English communication skills, both written and spoken

What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. At IST, we apply an office-first policy, meaning we primarily work from the office as we believe physical presence fosters collaboration, innovation, and a strong team spirit. At the same time, we understand the importance of flexibility—if you live farther away, working from the office three days a week with the remaining time remote may be possible. In Scandinavia our offices are located in Stockholm, Växjö, Roskilde and Oslo.

Interested in this role?

Apply Now

By applying, you agree to our privacy policy.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Energy Harvesting for Bio-Inspired Flying Robots
jobs.description:
The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics in Odense at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a PhD position in energy harvesting for bio-inspired flying robots. The position focuses on developing energy-harvesting techniques that use the magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines to support autonomous inspection of power lines. The starting date is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.  

This is a three-year PhD position based at SDU’s campus in Odense, Denmark.

The section focuses on conducting research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communication, utilizing cutting-edge reconfigurable computing and sensors. The aim is to develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions that solve technology-related challenges in fields such as autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grid, and healthcare.

The section contributes to our educational programmes in electrical engineering in Odense, offering Bachelor’s and Master of Science degrees in Electronics Engineering. Its activities span research, industrial collaboration, and education in electrical engineering and related areas.

The SDU campus in Odense comprises six faculties, bringing together academics and students in an environment that supports interdisciplinary research and a rich student life. Odense offers a vibrant robotics community, cultural activities, attractive residential areas, and green spaces along the river that runs through the city centre.

 

Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the FreeFly project, an ambitious research project focused on developing a bird-like flying robot for autonomous inspection of power lines. The PhD research will focus on energy harvesting to enable self-sustaining operation of this bio-inspired robotic platform.

Research Focus – Energy Harvesting for Bio-Inspired Flying Robots

You will investigate, analyse, and design novel energy-harvesting techniques that enable bio-inspired aerial robots to draw energy from the strong magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines. Your research will contribute to the development of self-sustaining flying robotic systems, with the aim of enabling extended autonomous inspection missions.

General Responsibilities

As a PhD student on this project, you will:

• 
Conduct research on energy harvesting from the magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines, contributing to the development of a self-sustaining, bird-like autonomous flying robot for inspection of power lines.

• 
Participate in teaching activities, including course planning and instruction in relevant subject areas.

• 
Collaborate closely with fellow PhD students, postdocs, and other members of the research group in a dynamic, interdisciplinary environment.

We are looking for a detail-oriented, self-driven candidate with a strong interest in energy harvesting and its application to bio-inspired flying robots. If you are motivated to contribute to innovative research in autonomous inspection of power lines, we encourage you to apply.

 

Required Qualifications

• 
A completed BSc and MSc in electronics, electrical engineering, physics, mechatronics, or a closely related discipline. Applicants in the final semester of their master’s programme are also encouraged to apply, provided they complete their MSc before the starting date and meet the applicable PhD admission requirements.

• 
Strong technical skills relevant to energy harvesting, particularly magnetic-field energy harvesting, electronics, and embedded hardware architectures.

• 
Demonstrated ability in academic writing, including preparing scientific reports, documentation, and research publications.

For further information about the position, please contact the Head of Digital and High-frequency Electronics section, Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, e-mail: esme@sdu.dk.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application that clearly explains the applicant’s interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages). 

• 
Detailed Curriculum Vitae, including personal contact information, skills, along with any other relevant information, e.g. teaching experience, computational skills, relevant projects, etc.

• 
Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation). Applicants in the final semester of their master’s programme are requested to submit transcripts from all completed semesters. 

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
Up to three names and emails of researchers who can provide an informed reference letter at short notice. (Reference letters and other relevant qualifications may also be included.)

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.313 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is from January 1, 2027.

jobs.description:
The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for an Assistant Professor position in Energy Harvesting and EMI Mitigation for Drones and Robots in High-Voltage Environments. The position is open from January 1, 2027, and the starting date will be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

Job Content

The Assistant Professor will conduct research within energy harvesting for drones, robotic systems, and IoT applications, with a particular focus on enhancing power density and enabling long-term autonomous operation. The research will further address electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) for electronic and robotic systems operating in extreme high-voltage environments, contributing to improved system reliability, safety, and performance in infrastructure inspection and maintenance applications.

The successful candidate is expected to develop and sustain a research agenda aligned with or complementing the section’s activities, establish an internationally recognized research profile, publish in high-impact journals and leading international conference proceedings, and actively contribute to securing external research funding from national and international sources. The role includes collaboration with academic colleagues and industrial partners and participation in national and international research activities.

The position includes planning, teaching, and developing Bachelor’s and Master’s-level courses in relevant areas of electronics and electrical engineering. The successful candidate will supervise Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD students, provide academic guidance, and contribute to a supportive and collaborative research and learning environment. The role also includes academic service at section and department levels and participation in relevant professional activities.

 

Required Qualifications

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in Electronics Engineering, Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field.

Applicants must document the following qualifications and experience:

• 
A strong research track record in electromagnetic energy harvesting, power conversion, or power management systems.

• 
Research experience in electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) for operation in extreme high-voltage environments up to 500 kV.

• 
Experience in the design, development, and testing of drone systems.

• 
Experience in university teaching, course development, and supervision of engineering students, together with pedagogical and subject-specific skills appropriate to the position.

• 
A proven ability to attract external research funding as principal investigator or key contributor.

• 
A strong publication record in leading international journals and conferences, including publications resulting from international collaborations.

• 
Demonstrated experience in international research projects and collaborative activities with academic and industrial partners.

• 
Experience serving as reviewer for leading international journals and conferences in relevant research fields.

International research experience gained in an environment other than the institution where the applicant completed their PhD will be considered an advantage.

 

Workplace description

The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics at the University of Southern Denmark conducts research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communications, using advanced reconfigurable computing and sensing technologies. The section develops next-generation electronics and computing solutions to address technological challenges in autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grids, and healthcare.

The section contributes to the electrical engineering programmes in Odense, including Bachelor’s and Master of Science degrees in Electronics Engineering. Over the next few years, the section is expected to expand to at least 30 staff members, including academic staff, PhD students, and engineers, supporting research, industrial collaboration, and education. This growth will strengthen the section’s contribution to electrical engineering and related fields.

SDU’s Odense campus comprises six faculties, providing opportunities for interdisciplinary research and a vibrant student life. Odense offers a culturally rich environment, a growing robotics community, attractive residential areas, and green spaces along the river through the city centre.

jobs.occupation: Better Nitrogen efficiency by improving Cow Resilience, Eating Dynamics, Breeding and Lifetime Efficiency
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Quantitative Genetics and Genomics programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Better Nitrogen efficiency by improving Cow Resilience, Eating Dynamics, Breeding and Lifetime Efficiency

Research area and project description
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) holds a leading position in cattle breeding research, particularly in genetic studies on data generated by advanced phenotyping technologies such as the CFIT 3D camera system through industry collaboration with VikingGenetics. This state-of-the-art system enables large-scale, non-invasive measurement of feed intake, body weight, and milk production data in over 30,000 cows directly in their production environment. This PhD project will leverage this extensive phenotypic dataset generated by CFIT, in combination with feeding parameters and other phenotypes from the Danish Cattle Database, to develop genetic tools aimed at enhancing nitrogen efficiency, resilience, eating dynamics and feed efficiency. The goal is to develop novel genomic breeding values for nitrogen efficiency, while considering other important breeding goal traits (e.g., productivity, health, fertility) and other traits, such as resilience, eating dynamics and feed efficiency. The project will apply advanced statistical methods, artificial intelligence, and cutting-edge genetic models to support and enhance management and breeding decision-making by dairy farmers. This project offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the green transition in agriculture by breeding cows that are both more sustainable and economically viable for the future of Danish dairy farming. We encourage candidates finishing their MSc in summer 2027 also to apply.

Qualifications and specific competences
A relevant master’s degree (120 ECTS) in Animal Breeding
Experience with data handling softwares (e.g., R, SAS, Python, Unix Shell) and genetic softwares (e.g., DMU, BLUPF90, AIREML).
Background in working with Livestock data is an advantage.
The ability to speak and write English fluently is a prerequisite for the applicant.
Can speak and write English fluently is a prerequisite.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C., Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Associate Professor Bingjie Li, e-mail: bingjie.li@qgg.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Tenure Track Assistant Professor Rasmus Bak Stephansen, e-mail: rasmus.stephansen@qgg.au.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
